covers: The write registers WR0 to WR7 and read registers RR0 to RR2 of one channel of the Z80 SIO, reached through the control port and the register pointer set by the last WR0 write

entries.name: RR0 status
entries.description: Per-channel status: receive and transmit buffers, modem input pins, transmit underrun and break latches.
entries.behaviour: Bit 0 receive character, bit 1 interrupt pending (channel A only), bit 2 transmit buffer empty, bit 3 DCD, bit 4 sync or hunt (RI on the DART), bit 5 CTS, bit 6 transmit underrun, bit 7 break or abort. Bits 3 to 5 read 1 for a low pin and latch on a change until Reset External/Status.

entries.name: RR1 special receive
entries.description: Special receive conditions of the oldest character in the receive FIFO, and the all-sent flag.
entries.behaviour: Bit 0 all sent (async: clear from a data write until sent; 1 in sync modes), bits 1 to 3 SDLC residue code, 4 parity error, 5 receive overrun, 6 CRC or framing error, 7 end of frame. On the SIO only bit 6 and the residue follow the FIFO head; bits 4, 5 and 7 stay until Error Reset.

entries.name: RR2 vector
entries.description: Interrupt vector, readable on channel B only; channel A reads 0.
entries.behaviour: Channel B returns its WR2, unchanged while WR1 bit 2 of channel B is clear. With it set, bits 1 to 3 hold the highest pending source: 0 to 3 for B transmit, external, receive, special receive, 4 to 7 the same for A, and 3 when none. Priority is A receive, A transmit, A external, then B's.

entries.name: WR0 command, pointer
entries.description: Selects the register of the next control access and carries the command and CRC reset fields.
entries.behaviour: Bits 0 to 2 name the register the next control read or write reaches, then the pointer returns to 0. Bits 3 to 5 are a command and bits 6 and 7 a CRC reset code (command entries). There is no point-high command, so registers 0 to 7 only are reachable; a read pointer above 2 returns 0.

entries.name: WR1 interrupt enable
entries.description: Interrupt enables, receive interrupt mode and the wait or ready pin function.
entries.behaviour: Bit 0 external/status interrupt enable, bit 1 transmit interrupt enable, bit 2 status affects vector (only channel B's counts), bits 3 and 4 receive interrupt mode: 0 off, 1 first character, 2 all with parity special, 3 all. Bit 5 wait or ready follows receive (1) or transmit (0), bit 6 ready (1) or wait (0), bit 7 enable.

entries.name: WR2 vector
entries.description: Interrupt vector value of the chip, kept on channel B.
entries.behaviour: Channel B's value is what RR2 of channel B returns and what interrupt acknowledge supplies, with bits 1 to 3 replaced by the source when WR1 bit 2 of channel B is set. Channel A's copy is stored and unused by MAME on the SIO.

entries.name: WR3 receive control
entries.description: Receiver enable, hunt and CRC controls, auto enables and receive character length.
entries.behaviour: Bit 0 receiver enable, 1 sync character load inhibit, 2 SDLC address search, 3 receive CRC enable, 4 enter hunt phase (sync modes), 5 auto enables (DCD gates the receiver, CTS the transmitter), bits 6 and 7 receive bits per character: 0 five, 1 seven, 2 six, 3 eight. Under auto enables a high DCD pin blocks reception.

entries.name: WR4 modes
entries.description: Parity, stop bits or synchronous mode, and the clock rate, shared by both directions.
entries.behaviour: Bit 0 parity enable, bit 1 even parity. Bits 2 and 3: 0 selects a synchronous mode, 1 one stop bit, 2 one and a half, 3 two. Bits 4 and 5, for sync only: 0 eight-bit sync, 1 sixteen-bit sync, 2 SDLC, 3 external sync; bits 6 and 7: clock x1, x16, x32, x64.

entries.name: WR5 transmit control
entries.description: Transmitter enable and character length, CRC controls, break and the RTS and DTR pins.
entries.behaviour: Bit 0 transmit CRC enable, 1 RTS, 2 CRC-16 (clear: CCITT), 3 transmitter enable, 4 send break, bits 5 and 6 bits per character (0 five, 1 seven, 2 six, 3 eight), 7 DTR. RTS and DTR pins are active low; in async mode clearing RTS raises it only after all sent. Clearing bit 3 clears the transmit interrupt.

sources.cites: case REG_WR5_TX_CONTROL:        do_sioreg_wr5(data); update_dtr_rts_break(); transmit_enable(); break;

entries.name: WR6 sync 1, address
entries.description: First transmit sync character in sync modes, or the SDLC station address.
entries.behaviour: Sent as the sync byte in eight-bit mode and first in sixteen-bit mode. Receive compares it as the first byte of a sixteen-bit sync and, in SDLC address search mode, as the station address (0xFF matches too). Stored and unused on the DART.

entries.name: WR7 sync 2, flag
entries.description: SDLC flag character, and the second sync character in sixteen-bit sync.
entries.behaviour: SDLC transmit sends it as the idle flag, so it should hold 0x7E when the transmitter is enabled. Receive matches it as the SDLC flag, as the eight-bit sync character and as the second byte of a sixteen-bit sync. Stored and unused on the DART.
